newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends with steep gains, cold temps near.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends with steep gains, cold temps near.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil and crude prices ended with steep gains Friday on short covering as a cold spell forecasted for the northeastern United States is expected to jump-start heating oil demand.
"More than anything else, this is short covering due to colder temperatures which could signal the start of winter," said Rita Beale, an analyst with Fimat USA Futures.
December heating oil ended 2.04 cents higher at 68.93 cents a gallon.
December crude settled up 85 cents at $23.59 a barrel and rose as high as $23.70.
Temperatures were forecasted to be 10 to 14 degrees below normal this weekend until the middle of next week in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
Though gasoline also posted sharp gains, they lagged the rest of the complex, with December gasoline ending up 1.47 cents a gallon at 65.27 cents.

Gasoline's rise was blunted on news an Illinois judge ruled Clark Refining and Marketing Co's Blue Island, Illinois refinery can stay open. A circuit court judge ruled the refinery had undergone "rigorous inspection," allowing the reopening of two units closed weeks ago by a fire.
Blue Island has an operating capacity of around 80,000 barrels per day (bpd), but was running at only 55,000 bpd since the two units were shut.

Pegasus Econometric Group analyst Tim Evans saw Friday's rally as an upside blip in an overall bear market. Analysts said the market expects heating oil supplies to meet demand, preventing a shortage and putting a cap on price gains.
A raft of short positions entered the market two weeks ago on news heating oil stocks were building amid record refinery output.
Traders said the rally in crude sharpened when buy programs were triggered after the price went above $23.00.
Traders also said crude prices received some support by a possible strike by oil workers of the state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela over privatization and benefit issues.
However, traders expected the issues to be resolved when union and state officials meet early next week.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
